correctness.rationale: The exact gamma-tail decomposition follows from independent exponential edge clocks on the two unique paths. For any n>=4, an alternative has greater SI-cut size and strictly better first derivative at t=0. Endpoints yield e^{-2βt} times a polynomial, whereas any other pair leaves an unmonitored endpoint, generating a >=e^{-βt}/n tail; this is uniform over finitely many alternatives and proves unique eventual endpoint optimality. P4 expressions cover all symmetry classes and their difference is e^{-2x}(e^x-1-2x)/4, with one strictly positive zero by convexity. n=3 and n=2 boundaries are checked. Full CTMC vs analytical formula passes 336 comparisons, plus 950 sampled inequalities and symbolic means; numerical evidence is not the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The fact a prior paper covers the same graph and sensor set under a different objective does not imply domination at every time. In the proved P4 case the two competing placements have equal exact means despite opposite finite-horizon rankings. Thus expectation-based theorems cannot establish the finite-deadline switch, nor does SIR early extinction provide the SI exponential tail. General optimization hardness does not imply an exact minimal graph classification.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary surveillance articles do not state or imply the claim. Christakis and Fowler (2010) measure empirical early warning, not uniform path two-sensor finite-time optima; Holme (2017) analyzes SIR mean detection/extinction times on small graphs, not an SI deadline distribution; Bai et al. (2017) investigate lead times in temporal empirical networks, with full text access incomplete; Holme (2018) studies single-sensor SIR objectives. Heavey et al. (2022) prove hardness and approximation for minimizing mean detection time, which does not imply the P4 finite-horizon switch when both policies have exactly equal means. No matching claim appears in the inspected research-record search or accessible related mathematical findings. Priority remains provisional because negative searches cannot prove global novelty.
residual_risks: No finite set of literature searches proves priority; classical reliability and continuous-time first-passage optimization literature might contain equivalent results.
The full original text of Bai et al. 2017 was unavailable during inspection; accessed excerpts do not justify a full-document exclusion.
Holme 2017 has extensive small-graph coverage under a different objective, increasing the need for independent comparison of any uninspected supplemental derivations.

value.rationale: Early-warning probability by a fixed intervention deadline is directly relevant to time-limited surveillance and can differ fundamentally from mean delay. The result proves a structural impossibility of a uniform two-sensor optimum on every path n>=4, gives a sharp n=4 cutoff and demonstrates equal mean detection times of strategies with reversed finite-deadline ranking. This is a natural complete minimal case plus an all-sizes theorem, not an arbitrary numerical slice. It does not claim clinical efficacy or any general-graph algorithm.
